blocks.text: By the end of this lesson you'll be able to read short rhythms of quarter and half notes and tap them in time, holding each note for its length. You'll also meet the whole note, and hold a key for its length at a real keyboard.

# Last time
A quick warm-up from last lesson: tap with the clicks, counting out loud, holding each tap until just before the next click. One set is plenty.

blocks.title: Warm-up: tap with the clicks
blocks.about: Tap with the clicks, counting out loud: one set is plenty.

blocks.text:
# When, and how long
Every note has two things: *when* it starts, and *how long* it lasts. So far each note was one beat long: press on the beat, hold, let go as the next beat comes. Now some notes will last longer than a beat. On the pad, a longer note means keeping your finger down for its whole length, and letting go just as the beat after it comes. The app checks both: a note let go well before its time is "let go early".

# Quarter notes and half notes
In the 4/4 music we're playing today, the shape of a note tells you how many beats it lasts.

A **quarter note** is a filled-in note head with a stem: **one beat**. Press on the count, hold, and let go as the next count comes, just as you did with the clicks.

A **half note** is an open (hollow) note head with a stem: **two beats**. Press on one count and keep your finger down through the next: count "1, 2" while you hold, and let go as the next beat arrives.

blocks.alt: In 4/4: a quarter note lasts 1 beat (filled head, stem), a half note 2 beats (open head, stem), a whole note 4 beats (open head, no stem)
blocks.caption: The three notes of this lesson, and how many beats each lasts in 4/4. The whole note comes at the end.

blocks.text: Rhythms here are written on a single line. The beats are grouped into **bars** (also called measures), divided by **bar lines**, the thin upright lines. The **4/4** at the start means four beats in every bar, each a quarter note long: count "1, 2, 3, 4" in every bar, and start again at 1 after each bar line.

blocks.alt: One bar of 4/4 on a one-line staff: quarter note on 1, quarter note on 2, half note on 3 held through 4, then a bar line
blocks.caption: Counting a bar: quarter, quarter, half. The half note starts on 3 and is held through 4.

blocks.text: The order that works for every new rhythm, the one Alfred's adult method asks for too: tap it and count it out loud first, then play it.

# Hear it, then tap it
Each card plays a short rhythm while you see it written, the pad lighting as it sounds. Then it counts you in, and you tap it back, counting aloud and holding each note its length. Take your time; the next step asks you to read them on your own.

blocks.title: Hear it, then tap it
blocks.about: Each card is played first, with the music in view; then you tap it back, holding each note its length.

blocks.text:
# Read it, then tap it
Now no sound first: each card appears and waits for you. Look across it and count it under your breath, "1, 2, 3–4" for instance, as long as you need. Then tap the pad (or press **Count in**): the app counts you in, and you tap the rhythm. A half note is easy to cut short: keep counting while you hold. If the app says a note was "let go early", that's the one to hold longer.

blocks.title: Read it, then tap it
blocks.about: Read each card at your own pace, then tap the pad to start its count-in and tap the rhythm.

blocks.text:
# The whole note
One more, just to meet it: the **whole note** is an open note head with no stem, and in 4/4 it lasts **four beats**, a whole bar. Press on "1" and keep your finger down through "2, 3, 4". The app plays each card first, with the music in view, then you tap it. It comes back in the lessons ahead.

blocks.title: Meet the whole note
blocks.about: Each card is played first; then tap it, holding a whole note through all four counts.

blocks.text:
# At a real keyboard: holding a note, letting it go on time
Last time you learned to play a key with a firm fingertip and let it go, so the key lifts your finger. Rhythm adds *when* you let go. For a half note, play on "1", keep the key down through "2", and let it go just as "3" comes. A half note let go too soon sounds like a quarter note with a gap after it.

Try it on a group of two black keys in the middle, right hand fingers 2 and 3 resting on the pair. Play finger 2 four times on "1, 2, 3, 4" (quarter notes); then finger 3 as two half notes ("1–2, 3–4"); then finger 2 as one whole note, held through all four counts. Count out loud. Then the same with your left hand's 2 and 3 on a pair further left. Keep the round hand from last time, and while you hold a long note keep your wrist soft rather than pressing harder.

# Make up a rhythm tune
Make up a little tune on the black keys with short notes and long ones. Count "1, 2, 3, 4" as you play and make it two bars long. A click keeps the beat for you, four to a bar; the **Click** button at the top turns it off if you'd rather count on your own. Play it a few times until it comes out the same way each time. Nothing is scored.

blocks.title: Make up a rhythm tune
blocks.about: A two-bar tune on the black keys with short and long notes, with the click, counting 1 to 4. Nothing is scored.

blocks.text:
# Check yourself
- Count "1, 2, 3, 4" aloud and tap your thigh: a quarter, a quarter, then a half note, keeping your hand pressed down through "3, 4". Did the half note last its two counts?
- In 4/4, how many beats does a half note last? A whole note?
- At a keyboard: play a half note and let it go exactly on "3". Did the key lift your finger, or did you pull it off?

# If this happens
- **Half notes come out too short.** Keep saying the second count while you hold: "1–2". Your finger leaves the pad on the next number, not before.
- **You lose your place in a card.** Look for the bar lines: each bar starts again on "1".
- **The app says "let go early" on quarter notes.** Keep your finger down until just before the next beat: a press, not a dab.
- **The app says you're late (or early) every time, by about the same amount.** Run the timing check again (Settings).

blocks.title: How to Count Basic Rhythms, Part 1 (The Mento Zone, 9 min)
blocks.caption: Counting quarter, half and whole notes, with drills. It also shows rests, which come later, on the five-line staff.
